Excellent! After **Rxd1+**, Black is up a full rook (+5 material). The main line is:

**Nxe3** (knight forks queen and rook) **fxe3 Rxd1+** and Black wins the rook, gaining material decisively.

**Motif:** Fork—the knight on e3 attacks both the queen and the undefended rook, forcing White's hand.

---

## Coaching Note

Your knight fork on e3 is the killer move here. It simultaneously attacks both the queen and rook—White cannot save both. After White recaptures with the f-pawn, you take the rook with check. **Key lesson:** When your opponent centralizes their pieces (queen and rook on exposed squares), look for jumps that fork multiple pieces. A well-placed knight in the center often finds two targets at once.
